newsitem.title: UK: British newspapers beat recycling target.
newsitem.headline: British newspapers beat recycling target.

text.p: Britain's newspaper industry has achieved voluntary recycling targets four years ahead of schedule, Environment Secretary John Gummer said on Tuesday.

In a statement Gummer said the industry's 1991 target of 40 percent recycled content in British newspapers by the year 2000 had been exceeded in the first half of 1996, when recycled content reached 41.2 percent.

He added that this "notable achievement" had been possible "by voluntary means and without government intervention or regulation." The industry has agreed a further range of initiatives, including publishing the recycled content of newsprint in a prominent position every day in order to encourage the public to continue to recycle papers.
